annotations.title: Check whether an agent may fetch a URL

description:
Says whether an AI agent may fetch a URL, on what terms, and at what price.
Reads robots.txt for a generic agent and for every AI user-agent the operators document,
the Content-signal and Content-Usage directives, any RSL licence the origin links, and
the live response to an honestly-identified request.

Verdicts: `allowed` (it served us), `allowed_if_identified` (the written policy permits
this but bot management refused an anonymous request — signing as a named crawler is the
documented route), `charged` (there is a price, quoted where the rail will show one),
`blocked` (the site disallows the agents that would want this, with nothing to buy), and
`unknown` (the origin did not answer, or the URL is not there).

Never evades: no CAPTCHA solving, no proxies, no spoofed user-agents. Refusals come back
as findings with the evidence attached.

includeEvidence.description: When true, the answer includes every request made, with status and headers (default false: it is large)

skipWellKnown.description: When true, the five well-known probes are skipped; faster, and those files are almost always absent

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to check, e.g. https://example.com/article
